title: Same lists, one switch
hook: Same six rankings, same rules. Does it matter which side makes the offers?

knows: ranking options from first to last
doesNotKnow: that in a matching market who proposes decides who gets their first choice
that deferred acceptance always ends stable

misconception: A stable matching procedure is neutral between the two sides.
objective: The learner can explain that the same rankings give different stable matchings depending on which side proposes, and that the proposing side gets its best stable partner.

Gale and Shapley 1962, College admissions and the stability of marriage, Amer. Math. Monthly 69(1), theorems 1 and 2 (proposer-optimality). · v5 (2026-10-14, demo-builder, learner r8 fit): reveal sentence cut to 'deferred acceptance always ends stable (Gale and Shapley 1962)'; 'gives the proposing side its best stable partner' dropped (learner r8 finding 5: told, not shown; and the word budget). Same source, theorem 1. Previous verdict void; needs re-check. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Verified by derivation, not by the unopened Gale and Shapley paper. Proof: if s and h prefer each other to their final partners, then s proposed to h before reaching its final partner (it proposes in rank order) and was turned down or bumped by h. A receiver only ever trades up, so h's final partner is better for h than s, a contradiction. Exhaustive check: all 6^6 = 46,656 3×3 profiles, each side proposing (93,312 runs), give 0 unstable matchings. Note: the reveal's attribution '(Gale and Shapley 1962)' is learner-facing but is in no claim, and its source was not opened (DNS).

The refused offer is drawn as a dashed line with a ✕ for the current run.

claims.text: Swapping which side proposes changes the pairs, and the side making offers does better in its own run (students: 2 first choices when they propose, 0 when hospitals do).
claims.source: Builder Python on the v4 example: students-proposing and hospitals-proposing matchings share no pair; every student strictly prefers their students-proposing partner, every hospital its hospitals-proposing partner. The reveal computes the sentence from the two recorded runs. Builder statement, not self-verified. | FC pass 26 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own check: the two matchings share no pair; Ann X>Y, Bea Y>Z, Cal Z>X (every student prefers the students-proposing partner); X Cal>Ann, Y Ann>Bea, Z Bea>Cal (every hospital prefers the hospitals-proposing partner). Students 2 first choices proposing, 0 receiving. Each mode has one outcome, so the reveal's 'Same pairs.' branch is unreachable and the 'different pairs, the side making offers did better' branch always prints.

recall.question: Two sides each rank the other. Running deferred acceptance twice on the same rankings, once with each side proposing, can give two different stable matchings. Which side does better in its own run?
recall.why: Deferred acceptance gives the proposing side its best stable partner, so switching who proposes can change who is happy.
